newsitem.title: INDIA: Pakistan business favours phased trade with India.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan business favours phased trade with India.

text.p: Pakistani business leaders on Monday called for phased trade liberalisation between India and Pakistan as a first step towards more open trade between the two nations, officials said.
"We can start gradually in a phased manner," Ilyas Ahmed Bilour, president of Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCCI), told a business meeting in New Delhi.

"The trade liberalisation should be phased in so that while India withdraws its subsidies and hidden incentives to exporters, Pakistan government can review its various policies so as to make our industrial sector competitive," he said.
Bilour added that trade worth $1.0 billion between the two nations took place through third countries and was not accounted under bilateral trade.
"We can bring this under bilateral trade," said A.S. Kasliwal, president of Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI).
The FPCCI and FICCI agreed to set up an expert panel to suggest ways, to their respective governments, to boost trade between the two nations.

The two way trade between India and Pakistan in 1995/96 (April-March) moved up to 4.07 billion rupees ($114 million) compared to 3.45 billion ($97 million) in the previous year, a FICCI statement said.

"The question of opening full-fledged trade with India is under active consideration of the government of Pakistan, after being signatory to World Trade Organisation and South Asian Preferential Trading Arrangement (SAPTA)," said Bilour.
Last week, foreign ministers from seven South Asian nations at the end of two days of discussions in New Delhi called for immediate launching of the third round of trade negotiations SAPTA.

The South Asian association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) comprises the Himalayan kingdoms of Bhutan and Nepal, the Indian Ocean island republics of Maldives and Sri Lanka, mostly Hindu India and its Moslem majority neighbours, Bangladesh and Pakistan.
Uneasy ties between India and Pakistan have overshadowed SAARC's efforts for a free trade bloc.
India has failed to win most favoured nation (MFN) trade status from arch-rival Pakistan.

India has already granted MFN status -- under which two countries undertake to give each other the maximum tariff concessions on their mutual trade which they already grant to other countries -- to all SAARC nations, including Pakistan.
